newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai automotive group considers stock listing.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai automotive group considers stock listing.

text.p: The Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp (Group) (SAIC), a major car producer in China, is considering a domestic or overseas stock listing for all or part of the group, a company official said on Tuesday.
"We are considering issuing stock for a listing, but we have not applied for state approval," Shen Jianhua, director of the president's office of the SAIC, told reporters at a briefing.
The company has not decided on the timing or location of a possible listing, but the Shanghai stock market is the most likely candidate since the company is located in the city, officials said.
They did not say whether the company hoped to issue domestic currency A shares or foreign currency B shares in China.

SAIC has a joint venture with Germany's Volkswagen AG which produces passenger cars in Shanghai, and recently signed an agreement with U.S. firm General Motors Corp to produce sedan cars through another joint venture based in the city.
SAIC's reported net profit in 1996 of 6.66 billion yuan.
